summary: Implemented stage 1 of the context efficiency plan: hard global character budget, stable prefix and mandatory integrity/freshness verification before planning.
completed_work: Recorded a four-stage improvement plan with primary research references.
Implemented full canonical instructions, budgeted optional sources and disclosed limitations.
Added pack integrity, prefix and source-hash verification to execution planning.
Added regression coverage for budgets, stable prefixes, stale sources, tampering and legacy drafts.
validation: Fourteen targeted tests passed, including the complete runtime lifecycle.
Final release profile passed all 46 gates, including 352 tests, 14 policies and cumulative/recovery/incremental package validation.
Whitespace diff review passed; provider cache and cost measurements remain outside stage 1.
decisions: Measure characters exactly; do not present them as token savings.
Keep canonical instructions whole and fail explicitly if the mandatory context cannot fit.
Require existing manifests to pass verification even when legacy draft mode is requested.
pending_work: Stage 2: select relevant sections and symbols instead of initial file excerpts.
Stage 3: add invalidated-by-content-hash local extraction reuse.
Stage 4: integrate runtime capabilities and measure actual tokens, cache usage, latency, cost and task acceptance.
risks: No provider prompt caching was enabled and no cost saving has been measured.
Context verification detects drift, not semantic completeness or malicious manifests.
Existing packs require rebuilding or explicit legacy draft mode.
next_action: Begin stage 2 with retrieval tests for relevant information located beyond the start of source files.
